entries.name: activity-action
entries.html: Set action on window activity when monitor-activity is on. any means activity in any window linked to a session causes a bell or message (depending on visual-activity) in the current window of that session, none means all activity is ignored (equivalent to monitor-activity being off), current means only activity in windows other than the current window are ignored and other means activity in the current window is ignored but not those in other windows.
entries.summary: Set action on window activity when monitor-activity is on.
entries.sourceText: Action to take on an activity alert.

entries.name: aggressive-resize
entries.html: Aggressively resize the chosen window. This means that tmux will resize the window to the size of the smallest or largest session (see the window-size option) for which it is the current window, rather than the session to which it is attached. The window may resize when the current window is changed on another session; this option is good for full-screen programs which support SIGWINCH and poor for interactive programs such as shells.
entries.summary: Aggressively resize the chosen window.
entries.sourceText: When 'window-size' is 'smallest', whether the maximum size of a window is the smallest attached session where it is the current window ('on') or the smallest session it is linked to ('off').

entries.name: allow-passthrough
entries.html: Allow programs in the pane to bypass tmux using a terminal escape sequence (\ePtmux;...\e\\). If set to on, passthrough sequences will be allowed only if the pane is visible. If set to all, they will be allowed even if the pane is invisible.
entries.summary: Allow programs in the pane to bypass tmux using a terminal escape sequence (\ePtmux;...\e\\).
entries.sourceText: Whether applications are allowed to use the escape sequence to bypass tmux. Can be 'off' (disallowed), 'on' (allowed if the pane is visible), or 'all' (allowed even if the pane is invisible).

entries.name: allow-rename
entries.html: Allow programs in the pane to change the window name using a terminal escape sequence (\ek...\e\\).
entries.summary: Allow programs in the pane to change the window name using a terminal escape sequence (\ek...\e\\).
entries.sourceText: Whether applications are allowed to use the escape sequence to rename windows.

entries.name: allow-set-title
entries.html: Allow programs in the pane to change the title using the terminal escape sequences (\e]2;...\e\\ or \e]0;...\e\\).
entries.summary: Allow programs in the pane to change the title using the terminal escape sequences (\e]2;...\e\\ or \e]0;...\e\\).
entries.sourceText: Whether applications are allowed to use the escape sequence to set the pane title.

entries.name: alternate-screen
entries.html: This option configures whether programs running inside the pane may use the terminal alternate screen feature, which allows the smcup and rmcupterminfo(5) capabilities. The alternate screen feature preserves the contents of the window when an interactive application starts and restores it on exit, so that any output visible before the application starts reappears unchanged after it exits.
entries.summary: This option configures whether programs running inside the pane may use the terminal alternate screen feature, which allows the smcup and rmcupterminfo(5) capabilities.
entries.sourceText: Whether applications are allowed to use the alternate screen.

entries.name: assume-paste-time
entries.html: If keys are entered faster than one in milliseconds, they are assumed to have been pasted rather than typed and tmux key bindings are not processed. The default is one millisecond and zero disables.
entries.summary: If keys are entered faster than one in milliseconds, they are assumed to have been pasted rather than typed and tmux key bindings are not processed.
entries.sourceText: Maximum time between input to assume it is pasting rather than typing.

entries.name: automatic-rename
entries.html:
Control automatic window renaming. When this setting is enabled, tmux will rename the window automatically using the format specified by automatic-rename-format. This flag is automatically disabled for an individual window when a name is specified at creation with new-window or new-session, or later with rename-window, or with a terminal escape sequence. It may be switched off globally with: 
set-option -wg automatic-rename off
entries.summary: Control automatic window renaming.
entries.sourceText: Whether windows are automatically renamed.

entries.name: automatic-rename-format
entries.html: The format (see FORMATS) used when the automatic-rename option is enabled.
entries.summary: The format (see FORMATS) used when the automatic-rename option is enabled.
entries.sourceText: Format used to automatically rename windows.

entries.name: backspace
entries.html: Set the key sent by tmux for backspace.
entries.summary: Set the key sent by tmux for backspace.
entries.sourceText: The key to send for backspace.

entries.name: base-index
entries.html: Set the base index from which an unused index should be searched when a new window is created. The default is zero.
entries.summary: Set the base index from which an unused index should be searched when a new window is created.
entries.sourceText: Default index of the first window in each session.

entries.name: bell-action
entries.html: Set action on a bell in a window when monitor-bell is on. The values are the same as those for activity-action.
entries.summary: Set action on a bell in a window when monitor-bell is on.
entries.sourceText: Action to take on a bell alert.

entries.name: buffer-limit
entries.html: Set the number of buffers; as new buffers are added to the top of the stack, old ones are removed from the bottom if necessary to maintain this maximum length.
entries.summary: Set the number of buffers; as new buffers are added to the top of the stack, old ones are removed from the bottom if necessary to maintain this maximum length.
entries.sourceText: The maximum number of automatic buffers. When this is reached, the oldest buffer is deleted.

entries.name: clock-mode-colour
entries.html: Set clock colour.
entries.summary: Set clock colour.
entries.sourceText: Colour of the clock in clock mode.

entries.name: clock-mode-style
entries.html: Set clock hour format.
entries.summary: Set clock hour format.
entries.sourceText: Time format of the clock in clock mode.

entries.name: codepoint-widths
entries.html: An array option allowing widths of Unicode codepoints to be overridden. Note the new width applies to all clients. Each entry is of the form codepoint=width, where codepoint may be a UTF-8 character, an identifier of the form ‘U+number’ where the number is a hexadecimal number, or a range of the form ‘U+number-U+number’.
entries.summary: An array option allowing widths of Unicode codepoints to be overridden.
entries.sourceText: Array of override widths for Unicode codepoints.

entries.name: command-alias
entries.html:
This is an array of custom aliases for commands. If an unknown command matches name, it is replaced with value. For example, after:
set -s command-alias[100] zoom='resize-pane -Z'

Using:

zoom -t:.1

Is equivalent to:

resize-pane -Z -t:.1

Note that aliases are expanded when a command is parsed rather than when it is executed, so binding an alias with bind-key will bind the expanded form.
entries.summary: This is an array of custom aliases for commands.
entries.sourceText: Array of command aliases. Each entry is an alias and a command separated by '='.

entries.name: copy-command
entries.html: Give the command to pipe to if the copy-pipe copy mode command is used without arguments.
entries.summary: Give the command to pipe to if the copy-pipe copy mode command is used without arguments.
entries.sourceText: Shell command run when text is copied. If empty, no command is run.

entries.name: copy-mode-current-line-number-style
entries.html: Set style of current line number in copy mode. For how to specify style, see the STYLES section.
entries.summary: Set style of current line number in copy mode.
entries.sourceText: Style of current line number in copy mode.

entries.name: copy-mode-current-match-style
entries.html: Set the style of the current search match in copy mode. For how to specify style, see the STYLES section.
entries.summary: Set the style of the current search match in copy mode.
entries.sourceText: Style of the current search match in copy mode.

entries.name: copy-mode-line-number-style
entries.html: Set style of line numbers in copy mode. For how to specify style, see the STYLES section.
entries.summary: Set style of line numbers in copy mode.
entries.sourceText: Style of line numbers in copy mode.

entries.name: copy-mode-line-numbers
entries.html: Show line numbers in copy mode. off hides line numbers, default shows line numbers matching the copy mode position indicator and goto-line, absolute shows absolute line numbers, relative shows line numbers relative to the cursor, and hybrid shows the current line number as absolute and other line numbers as relative. With off or default, the position indicator and goto-line use the same numbering; with absolute, relative and hybrid, they use absolute line numbers.
entries.summary: Show line numbers in copy mode.
entries.sourceText: Line number mode in copy mode.

entries.name: copy-mode-mark-style
entries.html: Set the style of the line containing the mark in copy mode. For how to specify style, see the STYLES section.
entries.summary: Set the style of the line containing the mark in copy mode.
entries.sourceText: Style of the marked line in copy mode.

entries.name: copy-mode-match-style
entries.html: Set the style of search matches in copy mode. For how to specify style, see the STYLES section.
entries.summary: Set the style of search matches in copy mode.
entries.sourceText: Style of search matches in copy mode.

entries.name: copy-mode-position-format
entries.html: Format of the position indicator in copy mode.
entries.summary: Format of the position indicator in copy mode.
entries.sourceText: Format of the position indicator in copy mode.

entries.name: copy-mode-position-style
entries.html: Set the style of the position indicator in copy mode. For how to specify style, see the STYLES section.
entries.summary: Set the style of the position indicator in copy mode.
entries.sourceText: Style of position indicator in copy mode.

entries.name: copy-mode-selection-style
entries.html: Set the style of the selection in copy mode. For how to specify style, see the STYLES section.
entries.summary: Set the style of the selection in copy mode.
entries.sourceText: Style of selection in copy mode.

entries.name: cursor-colour
entries.html: Set the colour of the cursor.
entries.summary: Set the colour of the cursor.
entries.sourceText: Colour of the cursor.

entries.name: cursor-style
entries.html: Set the style of the cursor. Available styles are: default, blinking-block, block, blinking-underline, underline, blinking-bar, bar.
entries.summary: Set the style of the cursor.
entries.sourceText: Style of the cursor.

entries.name: default-client-command
entries.html: Set the default command to run when tmux is called without a command. The default is new-session.
entries.summary: Set the default command to run when tmux is called without a command.
entries.sourceText: Default command to run when tmux is run without a command.

entries.name: default-command
entries.html: Set the command used for new windows (if not specified when the window is created) to shell-command, which may be any sh(1) command. The default is an empty string, which instructs tmux to create a login shell using the value of the default-shell option.
entries.summary: Set the command used for new windows (if not specified when the window is created) to shell-command, which may be any sh(1) command.
entries.sourceText: Default command to run in new panes. If empty, a shell is started.

entries.name: default-shell
entries.html: Specify the default shell. This is used as the login shell for new windows when the default-command option is set to empty, and must be the full path of the executable. When started tmux tries to set a default value from the first suitable of the SHELL environment variable, the shell returned by getpwuid(3), or /bin/sh. This option should be configured when tmux is used as a login shell.
entries.summary: Specify the default shell.
entries.sourceText: Location of default shell.

entries.name: default-size
entries.html: Set the default size of new windows when the window-size option is set to manual or when a session is created with new-session-d. The value is the width and height separated by an ‘x’ character. The default is 80x24.
entries.summary: Set the default size of new windows when the window-size option is set to manual or when a session is created with new-session-d.
entries.sourceText: Initial size of new sessions.

entries.name: default-terminal
entries.html: Set the default terminal for new windows created in this session - the default value of the TERM environment variable. For tmux to work correctly, this must be set to ‘screen’, ‘tmux’ or a derivative of them.
entries.summary: Set the default terminal for new windows created in this session - the default value of the TERM environment variable.
entries.sourceText: Default for the 'TERM' environment variable.

entries.name: destroy-unattached
entries.html: If on, destroy the session after the last client has detached. If off (the default), leave the session orphaned. If keep-last, destroy the session only if it is in a group and has other sessions in that group. If keep-group, destroy the session unless it is in a group and is the only session in that group.
entries.summary: If on, destroy the session after the last client has detached.
entries.sourceText: Whether to destroy sessions when they have no attached clients, or keep the last session whether in the group.

entries.name: detach-on-destroy
entries.html: If on (the default), the client is detached when the session it is attached to is destroyed. If off, the client is switched to the most recently active of the remaining sessions. If no-detached, the client is detached only if there are no detached sessions; if detached sessions exist, the client is switched to the most recently active. If previous or next, the client is switched to the previous or next session in alphabetical order.
entries.summary: If on (the default), the client is detached when the session it is attached to is destroyed.
entries.sourceText: Whether to detach when a session is destroyed, or switch the client to another session if any exist.

entries.name: display-panes-active-colour
entries.html: Set the colour used by the display-panes command to show the indicator for the active pane.
entries.summary: Set the colour used by the display-panes command to show the indicator for the active pane.
entries.sourceText: Colour of the active pane for 'display-panes'.

entries.name: display-panes-colour
entries.html: Set the colour used by the display-panes command to show the indicators for inactive panes.
entries.summary: Set the colour used by the display-panes command to show the indicators for inactive panes.
entries.sourceText: Colour of not active panes for 'display-panes'.

entries.name: display-panes-time
entries.html: Set the time in milliseconds for which the indicators shown by the display-panes command appear.
entries.summary: Set the time in milliseconds for which the indicators shown by the display-panes command appear.
entries.sourceText: Time for which 'display-panes' should show pane numbers.

entries.name: display-time
entries.html: Set the amount of time for which status line messages and other on-screen indicators are displayed. If set to 0, messages and indicators are displayed until a key is pressed. <var class="Ar">time</var> is in milliseconds.
entries.summary: Set the amount of time for which status line messages and other on-screen indicators are displayed.
entries.sourceText: Time for which status line messages should appear.

entries.name: editor
entries.html: Set the command used when tmux runs an editor.
entries.summary: Set the command used when tmux runs an editor.
entries.sourceText: Editor run to edit files.

entries.name: escape-time
entries.html: Set the time in milliseconds for which tmux waits after an escape is input to determine if it is part of a function or meta key sequences.
entries.summary: Set the time in milliseconds for which tmux waits after an escape is input to determine if it is part of a function or meta key sequences.
entries.sourceText: Time to wait before assuming a key is Escape.

entries.name: exit-empty
entries.html: If enabled (the default), the server will exit when there are no active sessions.
entries.summary: If enabled (the default), the server will exit when there are no active sessions.
entries.sourceText: Whether the server should exit if there are no sessions.

entries.name: exit-unattached
entries.html: If enabled, the server will exit when there are no attached clients.
entries.summary: If enabled, the server will exit when there are no attached clients.
entries.sourceText: Whether the server should exit if there are no attached clients.

entries.name: extended-keys
entries.html:
Controls how modified keys (keys pressed together with Control, Meta, or Shift) are reported. This is the equivalent of the modifyOtherKeysxterm(1) resource.

When set to on, the program inside the pane can request one of two modes: mode 1 which changes the sequence for only keys which lack an existing well-known representation; or mode 2 which changes the sequence for all keys. When set to always, modes 1 and 2 can still be requested by applications, but mode 1 will be forced instead of the standard mode. When set to off, this feature is disabled and only standard keys are reported.

tmux will always request extended keys itself if the terminal supports them. See also the extkeys feature for the terminal-features option, the extended-keys-format option and the pane_key_mode variable.
entries.summary: Controls how modified keys (keys pressed together with Control, Meta, or Shift) are reported.
entries.sourceText: Whether to request extended key sequences from terminals that support it.

entries.name: extended-keys-format
entries.html: Selects one of the two possible formats for reporting modified keys to applications. This is the equivalent of the formatOtherKeysxterm(1) resource. For example, C-S-a will be reported as ‘^[[27;6;65~’ when set to xterm, and as ‘^[[65;6u’ when set to csi-u.
entries.summary: Selects one of the two possible formats for reporting modified keys to applications.
entries.sourceText: The format of emitted extended key sequences.

entries.name: fill-character
entries.html: Set the character used to fill areas of the terminal unused by a window.
entries.summary: Set the character used to fill areas of the terminal unused by a window.
entries.sourceText: Character used to fill unused parts of window.

entries.name: focus-events
entries.html: When enabled, focus events are requested from the terminal if supported and passed through to applications running in tmux. Attached clients should be detached and attached again after changing this option.
entries.summary: When enabled, focus events are requested from the terminal if supported and passed through to applications running in tmux.
entries.sourceText: Whether to send focus events to applications.

entries.name: focus-follows-mouse
entries.html: When enabled and mouse is on, moving the mouse into a pane selects it.
entries.summary: When enabled and mouse is on, moving the mouse into a pane selects it.
entries.sourceText: Whether moving the mouse into a pane selects it.

entries.name: get-clipboard
entries.html:
Controls the behaviour when an application requests the clipboard from tmux.

If off, the request is ignored; if buffer, tmux responds with the newest paste buffer; request causes tmux to request the clipboard from the most recently used client (if possible) and send the reply (if any) back to the application; both is the same as request but also creates a paste buffer.

See also the set-clipboard option.
entries.summary: Controls the behaviour when an application requests the clipboard from tmux.
entries.sourceText: When an application requests the clipboard, whether to ignore the request ('off'); respond with the newest buffer ('buffer'); request the clipboard from the most recently used terminal ('request'); or to request the clipboard, create a buffer, and send it to the application ('both').

entries.name: history-file
entries.html: If not empty, a file to which tmux will write command prompt history on exit and load it from on start.
entries.summary: If not empty, a file to which tmux will write command prompt history on exit and load it from on start.
entries.sourceText: Location of the command prompt history file. Empty does not write a history file.

entries.name: history-limit
entries.html: Set the maximum number of lines held in pane history.
entries.summary: Set the maximum number of lines held in pane history.
entries.sourceText: Maximum number of lines to keep in the history for each pane. If changed, the new value applies only to new panes.

entries.name: initial-repeat-time
entries.html: Set the time in milliseconds for the initial repeat when a key is bound with the -r flag. This allows multiple commands to be entered without pressing the prefix key again. See also the repeat-time option. If initial-repeat-time is zero, repeat-time is used for the first key press.
entries.summary: Set the time in milliseconds for the initial repeat when a key is bound with the -r flag.
entries.sourceText: Time to wait for a key binding to repeat the first time the key is pressed, if it is bound with the '-r' flag. Subsequent presses use the 'repeat-time' option.

entries.name: input-buffer-size
entries.html: Maximum of bytes allowed to read in escape and control sequences. Once reached, the sequence will be discarded.
entries.summary: Maximum of bytes allowed to read in escape and control sequences.
entries.sourceText: Number of bytes accepted in a single input before dropping.

entries.name: key-table
entries.html: Set the default key table to key-table instead of root.
entries.summary: Set the default key table to key-table instead of root.
entries.sourceText: Default key table. Key presses are first looked up in this table.

entries.name: lock-after-time
entries.html: Lock the session (like the lock-session command) after number seconds of inactivity. The default is not to lock (set to 0).
entries.summary: Lock the session (like the lock-session command) after number seconds of inactivity.
entries.sourceText: Time after which a client is locked if not used.

entries.name: lock-command
entries.html: Command to run when locking each client. The default is to run lock(1) with -np.
entries.summary: Command to run when locking each client.
entries.sourceText: Shell command to run to lock a client.

entries.name: main-pane-height
entries.html: Set the width or height of the main (left or top) pane in the main-horizontal, main-horizontal-mirrored, main-vertical, or main-vertical-mirrored layouts. If suffixed by ‘%’, this is a percentage of the window size.
entries.summary: Set the width or height of the main (left or top) pane in the main-horizontal, main-horizontal-mirrored, main-vertical, or main-vertical-mirrored layouts.
entries.sourceText: Height of the main pane in the 'main-horizontal' layout. This may be a percentage, for example '10%'.

entries.name: main-pane-width
entries.html: Set the width or height of the main (left or top) pane in the main-horizontal, main-horizontal-mirrored, main-vertical, or main-vertical-mirrored layouts. If suffixed by ‘%’, this is a percentage of the window size.
entries.summary: Set the width or height of the main (left or top) pane in the main-horizontal, main-horizontal-mirrored, main-vertical, or main-vertical-mirrored layouts.
entries.sourceText: Width of the main pane in the 'main-vertical' layout. This may be a percentage, for example '10%'.

entries.name: menu-border-lines
entries.html: Set the type of characters used for drawing menu borders. See popup-border-lines for possible values for border-lines.
entries.summary: Set the type of characters used for drawing menu borders.
entries.sourceText: Type of characters used to draw menu border lines. Some of these are only supported on terminals with UTF-8 support.

entries.name: menu-border-style
entries.html: Set the menu border style. See the STYLES section on how to specify style.
entries.summary: Set the menu border style.
entries.sourceText: Default style of menu borders.

entries.name: menu-selected-style
entries.html: Set the selected menu item style. See the STYLES section on how to specify style.
entries.summary: Set the selected menu item style.
entries.sourceText: Default style of selected menu item.

entries.name: menu-style
entries.html: Set the menu style. See the STYLES section on how to specify style.
entries.summary: Set the menu style.
entries.sourceText: Default style of menu.

entries.name: message-command-style
entries.html: Set status line message command style. This is used for the command prompt with vi(1) keys when in command mode. For how to specify style, see the STYLES section.
entries.summary: Set status line message command style.
entries.sourceText: Style of the command prompt when in command mode, if 'mode-keys' is set to 'vi'.

entries.name: message-format
entries.html: Set the format string for the prompt and message area. The special placeholder ‘#{message}’ expands to the interactive prompt or message text and ‘#{command_prompt}’ is set to 1 when the prompt is in command mode (vi). Style directives like fill, align, and width may be used in the format string. The default uses a conditional to select between message-style and message-command-style.
entries.summary: Set the format string for the prompt and message area.
entries.sourceText: Format string for the prompt and message area. The '#{message}' placeholder is replaced with the content.

entries.name: message-limit
entries.html: Set the number of error or information messages to save in the message log for each client.
entries.summary: Set the number of error or information messages to save in the message log for each client.
entries.sourceText: Maximum number of server messages to keep.

entries.name: message-line
entries.html: Set line on which status line messages and the command prompt are shown.
entries.summary: Set line on which status line messages and the command prompt are shown.
entries.sourceText: Position (line) of messages and the command prompt.

entries.name: message-style
entries.html: Set status line message style. This is used for messages and for the command prompt. The message is drawn on top of the existing status line. A width attribute (a fixed number of columns or a percentage such as ‘50%’) constrains the prompt area width and an align attribute (left, centre, right) sets its horizontal position. When the width is less than the full terminal width, the normal status bar content remains visible around the prompt area. The fill attribute is used by the default message-format to clear the background. For how to specify style, see the STYLES section.
entries.summary: Set status line message style.
entries.sourceText: Style of messages and the command prompt. A 'fill' attribute controls background clearing and a 'width' attribute (fixed or percentage) constrains the prompt area width.

entries.name: mode-keys
entries.html: Use vi or emacs-style key bindings in copy mode. The default is emacs, unless VISUAL or EDITOR contains ‘vi’.
entries.summary: Use vi or emacs-style key bindings in copy mode.
entries.sourceText: Key set used in copy mode.

entries.name: mode-style
entries.html: Set window modes style. For how to specify style, see the STYLES section.
entries.summary: Set window modes style.
entries.sourceText: Style of indicators and highlighting in modes.

entries.name: monitor-activity
entries.html: Monitor for activity in the window. Windows with activity are highlighted in the status line.
entries.summary: Monitor for activity in the window.
entries.sourceText: Whether an alert is triggered by activity.

entries.name: monitor-bell
entries.html: Monitor for a bell in the window. Windows with a bell are highlighted in the status line.
entries.summary: Monitor for a bell in the window.
entries.sourceText: Whether an alert is triggered by a bell.

entries.name: monitor-silence
entries.html: Monitor for silence (no activity) in the window within interval seconds. Windows that have been silent for the interval are highlighted in the status line. An interval of zero disables the monitoring.
entries.summary: Monitor for silence (no activity) in the window within interval seconds.
entries.sourceText: Time after which an alert is triggered by silence. Zero means no alert.

entries.name: mouse
entries.html: If on, tmux captures the mouse and allows mouse events to be bound as key bindings. See the MOUSE SUPPORT section for details.
entries.summary: If on, tmux captures the mouse and allows mouse events to be bound as key bindings.
entries.sourceText: Whether the mouse is recognised and mouse key bindings are executed. Applications inside panes can use the mouse even when 'off'.

entries.name: other-pane-height
entries.html: Set the height of the other panes (not the main pane) in the main-horizontal and main-horizontal-mirrored layouts. If this option is set to 0 (the default), it will have no effect. If both the main-pane-height and other-pane-height options are set, the main pane will grow taller to make the other panes the specified height, but will never shrink to do so. If suffixed by ‘%’, this is a percentage of the window size.
entries.summary: Set the height of the other panes (not the main pane) in the main-horizontal and main-horizontal-mirrored layouts.
entries.sourceText: Height of the other panes in the 'main-horizontal' layout. This may be a percentage, for example '10%'.

entries.name: other-pane-width
entries.html: Like other-pane-height, but set the width of other panes in the main-vertical and main-vertical-mirrored layouts.
entries.summary: Like other-pane-height, but set the width of other panes in the main-vertical and main-vertical-mirrored layouts.
entries.sourceText: Height of the other panes in the 'main-vertical' layout. This may be a percentage, for example '10%'.

entries.name: pane-active-border-style
entries.html: Set the pane border style for the currently active pane. For how to specify style, see the STYLES section. Attributes are ignored.
entries.summary: Set the pane border style for the currently active pane.
entries.sourceText: Style of the active pane border.

entries.name: pane-base-index
entries.html: Like base-index, but set the starting index for pane numbers.
entries.summary: Like base-index, but set the starting index for pane numbers.
entries.sourceText: Index of the first pane in each window.

entries.name: pane-border-format
entries.html: Set the text shown in pane border status lines.
entries.summary: Set the text shown in pane border status lines.
entries.sourceText: Format of text in the pane status lines.

entries.name: pane-border-indicators
entries.html: Indicate active pane by colouring only half of the border in windows with exactly two panes, by displaying arrow markers, by drawing both or neither.
entries.summary: Indicate active pane by colouring only half of the border in windows with exactly two panes, by displaying arrow markers, by drawing both or neither.
entries.sourceText: Whether to indicate the active pane by colouring border or displaying arrow markers.

entries.name: pane-border-lines
entries.html:
Set the type of characters used for drawing pane borders. type may be one of:
single
single lines using ACS or UTF-8 characters
double
double lines using UTF-8 characters
heavy
heavy lines using UTF-8 characters
simple
simple ASCII characters
number
the pane number
spaces
space characters

‘double’ and ‘heavy’ will fall back to standard ACS line drawing when UTF-8 is not supported.
entries.summary: Set the type of characters used for drawing pane borders.
entries.sourceText: Type of characters used to draw pane border lines. Some of these are only supported on terminals with UTF-8 support.

entries.name: pane-border-status
entries.html: Turn pane border status lines off or set their position.

entries.name: pane-scrollbars
entries.html:
When enabled, a character based scrollbar appears on the left or right of each pane. A filled section of the scrollbar, known as the ‘slider’, represents the position and size of the visible part of the pane content.

If set to on the scrollbar is visible all the time. If set to modal the scrollbar only appears when the pane is in copy mode or view mode. When the scrollbar is visible, the pane is narrowed by the width of the scrollbar and the text in the pane is reflowed. If set to modal, the pane is narrowed only when the scrollbar is visible.

See also pane-scrollbars-style.

entries.html:
Attempt to set the terminal clipboard content using the xterm(1) escape sequence, if there is an Ms entry in the terminfo(5) description (see the TERMINFO EXTENSIONS section).

If set to on, tmux will both accept the escape sequence to create a buffer and attempt to set the terminal clipboard. If set to external, tmux will attempt to set the terminal clipboard but ignore attempts by applications to set tmux buffers. If off, tmux will neither accept the clipboard escape sequence nor attempt to set the clipboard.

Note that this feature needs to be enabled in xterm(1) by setting the resource:

disallowedWindowOps: 20,21,SetXprop

Or changing this property from the xterm(1) interactive menu when required.

entries.name: terminal-features
entries.html:
Set terminal features for terminal types read from terminfo(5). tmux has a set of named terminal features. Each will apply appropriate changes to the terminfo(5) entry in use.

tmux can detect features for a few common terminals; this option can be used to easily tell tmux about features supported by terminals it cannot detect. The terminal-overrides option allows individual terminfo(5) capabilities to be set instead, terminal-features is intended for classes of functionality supported in a standard way but not reported by terminfo(5). Care must be taken to configure this only with features the terminal actually supports.

This is an array option where each entry is a colon-separated string made up of a terminal type pattern (matched using glob(7) patterns) followed by a list of terminal features. The available features are:

256
Supports 256 colours with the SGR escape sequences.
clipboard
Allows setting the system clipboard.
ccolour
Allows setting the cursor colour.
cstyle
Allows setting the cursor style.
extkeys
Supports extended keys.
focus
Supports focus reporting.
hyperlinks
Supports OSC 8 hyperlinks.
ignorefkeys
Ignore function keys from terminfo(5) and use the tmux internal set only.
margins
Supports DECSLRM margins.
mouse
Supports xterm(1) mouse sequences.
osc7
Supports the OSC 7 working directory extension.
overline
Supports the overline SGR attribute.
progressbar
Supports the OSC 9;4 progress bar extension.
rectfill
Supports the DECFRA rectangle fill escape sequence.
RGB
Supports RGB colour with the SGR escape sequences.
sixel
Supports SIXEL graphics.
strikethrough
Supports the strikethrough SGR escape sequence.
sync
Supports synchronized updates.
title
Supports xterm(1) title setting.
usstyle
Allows underscore style and colour to be set.
entries.summary: Set terminal features for terminal types read from terminfo(5).
entries.sourceText: List of terminal features, used if they cannot be automatically detected.

entries.name: terminal-overrides
entries.html:
Allow terminal descriptions read using terminfo(5) to be overridden. Each entry is a colon-separated string made up of a terminal type pattern (matched using glob(7) patterns) and a set of name=value entries.

For example, to set the ‘clear’ terminfo(5) entry to ‘\e[H\e[2J’ for all terminal types matching ‘rxvt*’:

rxvt*:clear=\e[H\e[2J

The terminal entry value is passed through strunvis(3) before interpretation.
entries.summary: Allow terminal descriptions read using terminfo(5) to be overridden.
entries.sourceText: List of terminal capabilities overrides.
